page: Amazon Web Services r6in.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. It provides 256 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance features a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance shows consistent multi-threaded compute and data handling performance. It achieved a multi-core stress-ng result of 30,929.24, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 139.8 GB/s and write bandwidth of 66.88 GB/s. In-memory throughput reached 30.91 million Redis SET operations per second, supported by a static web serving rate of 34.51 GB/s. Language model inference execution reached 298.34 tokens per second on small 135M parameter models, but execution slowed to 5.91 tokens per second on large 70B parameter models.

From a cost and architecture perspective, the instance provides high RAM density relative to its compute core allocation, making it efficient for workloads requiring large resident datasets without purchasing excess compute cores. Because local storage is absent, persistent storage relies entirely on network-attached storage architectures utilizing the 50 Gbps network pipe. The instance fits in-memory caching systems, relational databases, distributed data processing, and large-scale enterprise analytics.
